correctness.rationale: For rooted uniform recursive attachment P_t uniform in {1,...,t-1}, terminal means no children (root excluded). For an old nonroot terminal indicator I_v and parent terminal-child counts ell_v, the exact increments are Delta L=1-I_V and Delta C=ell_V-I_V(ell_{P_V}-1), giving conditional moments E Delta L=1-L/n, E Delta C=(L-2C)/n, and E(Delta L Delta C)=L/n. Expand L^2 and LC to obtain four triangular moment recurrences; n=2,3 bases produce E L=n/2, E C=n/6 (n>=3), Var L=n/12 (n>=3), E LC=n^2/12+n/8 and Cov(L,C)=n/8 (n>=4). The individual sibling-pair probability for 2<=i<j<=n is (i-1)/((n-1)(n-2)), from shared-parent choice, exclusion of later attachments to i, and exclusion of both children after j. Independent exhaustive enumeration of all rooted recursive parent vectors for n=2..7 recovered covariance 0,1/4,n/8 and the age-index probabilities; these finite tests corroborate, not prove, all n. The least-squares regression slope is n/8 divided by n/12 =3/2, not the conditional expectation slope.

value.rationale: An exact all-n mixed covariance measures dependence of global terminal abundance on sibling aggregation, a genuine local-versus-global random recursive tree question. The n-independent least-squares coefficient and birth-order-resolved probabilities give structural, reusable identities beyond the classical one-variable leaf-count mean/variance. Rooted terminal and unordered-pair conventions are essential; no full joint law or monotonic regression is claimed.

limitations: Every n>=4, with explicit n=2,3 exceptions, uniformly independent older-parent attachment; rooted outdegree-zero leaves, all sibling pairs; no Yule/Cayley extension.
